about.title: Lincoln Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Lincoln has grown quickly, and with that growth comes more retail centers, apartment communities, and public walkways along corridors like Ferrari Ranch Road and Joiner Parkway. When a property owner lets a hazard go unaddressed — a wet floor, broken stair, uneven parking lot, or poor lighting — the people who get hurt are often left figuring out medical care, missed work, and an insurance company that wants a recorded statement fast. Premises liability claims in California hinge on what the owner knew, or should have known, and whether they had a fair chance to fix or warn about the danger. That makes early evidence, especially surveillance footage that businesses often overwrite within days, critical. We handle premises liability claims and can evaluate what happened, gather the right records, and explain your options in plain terms, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Evidence Matter in a Lincoln Fall Case

items.title: Notice Has to Be Shown
items.desc: California law requires proof the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard before your fall. We can help track down maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that speak to that.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Lincoln retailers and property managers overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having video evidence and having none.

items.title: Your Deadline May Be Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: Most premises liability claims in California must be filed within two years, but claims against a government-owned property carry a much tighter window. If your fall happened on public property in Lincoln, don't wait to find out which deadline applies.

items.question: I fell at a store on Lincoln Boulevard — do I have a case?
items.answer: It depends on whether the hazard that caused your fall was something the store knew about or should have discovered through reasonable inspection. We can review the details, including any incident report filed at the time, to help you understand where things stand. There's no cost to have your situation looked at.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my own fall?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame, though your amount may be reduced by your percentage of fault. This is decided case by case based on the specific facts. We can walk you through how that might apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after a fall in Lincoln?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of injury to file a premises liability claim, but claims involving a public entity, such as a city-owned sidewalk or building, often require formal notice within a much shorter window. Because Lincoln has both private businesses and public facilities, it's worth having us confirm which timeline applies to your fall as soon as possible.
